2.translation: ## Count observations or display supplied values ⟦shared:0⟧

3.translation:
⟦shared:0⟧ counts observations at source positions; ⟦shared:1⟧ displays supplied values.
Each accession/window computes its Stat and data Position before view projection
or display replication. ⟦shared:2⟧ selects the physical band;
⟦shared:3⟧ independently selects a native data adjustment such as stack or dodge.
The earlier ⟦shared:4⟧ band spelling remains accepted.

6.translation: The shortcut below counts the same observations using the same physical band.

10.translation: | bar | count | x/pos observations, optional weight |

11.translation: | col | identity | supplied y/track_value; interval or position |

12.translation: | point, line, path, step, text | identity | source x and local y; text requires label |

13.translation: | tile, rect, area, ribbon, segment, linerange, errorbar | identity | corresponding native ggplot2 extents |

14.translation:
Available statistics are identity/count/bin/summary, plus the documented [smooth/density/ecdf estimation combinations](⟦shared:0⟧). Bin needs explicit binwidth
or breaks. Native group and after_stat mappings are supported; numerical axes
retain the statistic's value units. Arbitrary third-party Geom/Stat plugins and
unsupported combinations are rejected. Existing
track line/tile shortcuts retain their documented behaviour.

15.translation: Source position uses x orientation; native text size currently uses mm and polygon outlines are full. Other orientations/size units/partial outlines fail explicitly. Native text styles and path arrows are forwarded.

16.translation: Native tracks currently require one panel and a ggchord coordinate system. Facets, ⟦shared:0⟧, raster, boxplot and violin are outside this first supported set and are rejected explicitly. Use ⟦shared:1⟧ for vertical projection. Statistical source membership is preserved before dodge or other data positions. Rectangles and tiles use their supplied bounds without an artificial zero baseline.

17.translation: ## Two independent bands and display order ⟦shared:0⟧

18.translation: Encode the same GC by bar height and colour using explicit gc_height/gc_colour IDs. Set height and colour domains 0–1 separately, with distinct physical widths. The second figure changes only colour order from 2 to 0, moving that band nearer the backbone. Order is a finite priority, not a measurement or required one-based index; ties use IDs. Layers sharing an ID must agree on side/order/width/gap. Lines do not implicitly bridge independent windows.

25.translation: GC here is ⟦shared:0⟧: ambiguous bases remain in the denominator and contribute zero to the numerator. The final window uses its actual number of bases. This pUC19 input has no ambiguous bases; for other inputs explicitly choose and report a policy rather than assuming they are omitted. Focusing clips intervals and retains the original summary; it does not recompute GC for a shortened window. Line tracks connect the supplied samples within their grouping; ⟦shared:1⟧ explicitly controls circular closure and ⟦shared:2⟧ belongs to physical track placement. Do not use a closed line to imply continuity across omitted source windows.

27.translation: ⟦shared:0⟧ also delegates ⟦shared:1⟧, ⟦shared:2⟧ and ⟦shared:3⟧ to native ggplot2 statistics **before projection**. These create estimates of supplied observations, not additional observations. They run independently by accession/window and explicit group. Estimation ⟦shared:4⟧ records the eligible group submitted to the estimator after native missing-value handling; it is not per-point influence, positive read support or a custom model's additional internal filtering report.

33.translation: Other combinations of these statistics fail explicitly. Use ⟦shared:0⟧ explicitly for density area because area otherwise defaults to stacking. ⟦shared:1⟧ remains the Track source-boundary policy and does not forward the native density boundary-correction parameter. Facets, boxplots, violins, raster and arbitrary third-party Geom/Stat objects remain unsupported; a numerical name in a function is not a projection contract.

34.translation: Reuse the real ⟦shared:0⟧ and ⟦shared:1⟧ prepared above. This explicit linear fit is a display summary of the GC fractions, with a native confidence ribbon and mean line sharing one Track:

36.translation: Statistical fitting uses raw supplied source x/y. A later transformed Track value scale maps the estimates; it does not silently refit a log-space model, unlike placing a transform before a Stat in a native ggplot. If transformed-space fitting is intended, prepare and name that transformed variable explicitly and state its unit. Kernel density of event positions is not measured sequencing depth. ECDF output is a cumulative distribution, not a basewise alignment.

37.translation: The directed source-backed checks compare native ggplot2 results and group membership for real pUC19 GC windows and G/C positions, plus curved/vertical projection and an explicitly missing-value control. ⟦shared:0⟧ retains the numerical report and actual CI/mean image. Finite source bounds and physical-band constraints still apply; automatic placement does not change the fitted model or manufacture observations.

38.translation: ## Tracks and windows share source coordinates ⟦shared:0⟧

39.translation: Focus pUC19 to 500–1500 bp and trim the same observed GC windows as intervals. `focus_ggchord_track` does not recompute averages, invent boundary samples or bridge omitted windows. Return to actual DNA and declare new windows/denominators if finer GC summaries are needed.
